History:
- Chief complaint: Recurrent severe headaches with associated symptoms including feeling hot, reduced appetite, weight loss, tingling in the arms, palpitations, and shortness of breath.
- Onset/duration: Symptoms began roughly when patient changed jobs; headaches occur during work (meetings or laptop use) and come/go; other symptoms vary in time, not all occurring simultaneously.
- Progression/context: Symptoms are ongoing and affecting work; stress level high (estimated 7–8/10).
- Associated factors: Headache described as frontal/over the head; nausea mild; episodes occur mainly at work; shortness of breath at desk; tingling in both arms; heart rate sensations described as fast beating; libido decreased since job change.
- Triggers/setting: Primarily at work/computer use; reclines to desk and meetings.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic condition: Hyperthyroidism.
- Medications: Thyroxine (dose/frequency not documented); patient denies other medications.
- Allergies: None documented.
- Other: Tobacco use not specified; alcohol use: weekly, a couple of glasses of wine.
- Prior hospitalizations: none documented.

Physical Examination:
- Not conducted yet; no physical findings documented in transcript.

Impression:
- Evaluation for new intermittent headaches with autonomic/cardiopulmonary symptoms in a patient with known hyperthyroidism; clinical status currently undetermined pending in-person exam and laboratory testing.

Management Plan:
- Arrange in-clinic examination with a physician to assess heart and lung function.
- Obtain blood tests, including thyroid function (thyroxine level) and related labs.
- No new medications prescribed today; in-person assessment needed before treatment decisions.
- Appointment to be booked via app; clinician will be informed of patient history prior to visit.

Patient Summary:
- A 35-year-old lawyer with hyperthyroidism presents with intermittent headaches, weight loss, reduced appetite, tingling in both arms, and occasional palpitations/dyspnea, onset after changing jobs. Plan is an in-person clinic evaluation with heart/lung exam and thyroid function testing to guide management.

Key Takeaways:
- Schedule an in-person clinic visit for comprehensive exam and blood tests (thyroid function).
- Report any worsening symptoms (increasing headaches, greater weight loss, chest symptoms, or shortness of breath).
- No medications started until after the in-person assessment.

Next Steps:
- In-person clinic assessment and physical examination.
- Blood tests including thyroxine (and other thyroid function tests) to reassess thyroid status.
- Follow-up planned after results to determine appropriate management.

  - Allergies: none documented.
  - Medications: thyroxine noted; dose, route, and frequency not documented.
  - Vitals: not provided.
  - Comprehensive medication reconciliation and prior hospitalizations not detailed beyond current meds.
- Internal conflicts: None noted.
